newsitem.title: USA: New York sues FCC over pay phone deregulation.
newsitem.headline: New York sues FCC over pay phone deregulation.

text.p: Fearing higher pay telephone charges, the New York Public Services Commission said Tuesday it filed suit challenging a Federal Communications Commission order deregulating pay phone rates.
The FCC order, made in September, would let the market set pay phone rates across the country from October 1997.
"While we support the introduction of competition in New York's telecommunications industry, we must ensure consumers will benefit," John O'Mara, state commission chairman, said Tuesday.
"In this case, the decision to deregulate coin phone rates seems likely to yield higher rates unless certain issues are addressed," he said.
The suit was filed Monday in U.S. Court of Appeals in Washington, following the denial of an earlier petition, the commission said.
The commission said that deregulation should wait for evidence that a competitive marketplace exists, and should protect pay phone users from monopolies in key areas.
It predicted the FCC order would only result in competition at premium locations. It said that restaurants and bars, for example, were likely to have just one pay phone.
Regional Bell telephone companies are the predominant providers of pay phone service across the country, though in many states there are competitors.

Nynex Corp., for example, faces competition from Teleport Communications Group Inc. and about 50 smaller companies in New York State. A state commission spokesman said that other states have suits pending against the pay phone ruling.
